headline: Westmoreland Athletic cruise past Highland Park in Matchweek 17
dek: Westmoreland Athletic ran out 3-0 winners at Royal Ground, with Dante Russo among the scorers.
author: Priya Nair
body: Westmoreland Athletic claimed a 3-0 win over Highland Park in front of 14,689 at Royal Ground, a result that keeps the Matchweek 17 talking points coming.
The goals came from Dante Russo (1'), Sean Bennett (15') and Mohammed Korhonen (67').
The hosts saw 66% of the ball, registering 12 shots to the visitors' 7, and referee D. Whitlock kept the game flowing (9°C, light rain).
Westmoreland Athletic will feel the scoreline was a fair reflection of the contest, while Highland Park head home knowing the margins at this level remain unforgiving.
Attention now turns to the next round of fixtures, with both camps expected to rotate as the schedule tightens.

headline: Harborside United stretch clear at the summit
dek: Harborside United lead the way on 42 points, but Saint Mary's FC and Westmoreland Athletic are refusing to let the title race settle.
author: Priya Nair
body: With the business end of the season in view, Harborside United sit top of the Atlantic Coast Premier League on 42 points from 17 games — a record of 13 wins, 3 draws and just 1 defeat.
Behind them, Saint Mary's FC (34 pts) and Westmoreland Athletic (32 pts) are refusing to blink, while Harborside United's goal difference of +36 is the division's best by some distance.
The chasing pair meet each other once more before the season is out, meaning the leaders may only need to hold serve at home to keep the destiny of the title in their own hands.
History urges caution: leads have evaporated at this stage before, and the fixture computer has saved several of the leaders' hardest away days for the run-in.
What is beyond argument is that the front three have separated themselves from the pack — fourth place is already 2 points off the podium.

headline: Idris Riley leads the Golden Boot race
dek: Idris Riley of Albion FC tops the scoring charts with 10 goals this season.
author: Matt Crain
body: Idris Riley has been the league's standout finisher, with 10 goals in 7 appearances leaving the Albion FC man at the top of the charts.
The chasing pack is close behind: Mateo Reyes (8) and Stefan Korhonen (6) can each overhaul the leader with one hot streak.
What separates the front-runner is consistency — goals spread across the season rather than bunched in a single purple patch.
With 5 matchweeks remaining, the Golden Boot may yet come down to which contender's side creates more in the final stretch.

headline: The fight to beat the drop goes to the wire
dek: Bridgeport FC, Marshall Town and Oakvale Wanderers are locked in a scrap at the foot of the table.
author: Tom Beckett
body: Only 4 points separate Bridgeport FC in tenth from Oakvale Wanderers at the foot of the table — the tightest bottom three the league has seen in years.
Oakvale Wanderers's problem is at both ends: 7 scored, 31 conceded, and a goal difference of -24 that could yet decide their fate on the final day.
Marshall Town have shown flashes — 2 wins says they can live at this level — but back-to-back results have proven elusive.
The remaining head-to-heads between the bottom sides now look like cup finals; six-pointers is an overused phrase, but here it fits.
Two go down. Nobody in the bottom four can afford to look away.

headline: “We take it one game at a time”: Petra Yilmaz on the title run-in
dek: The Harborside United manager reflects on a season that has the club dreaming of the trophy.
author: Priya Nair
body: Petra Yilmaz sat down with us to talk through the season so far and what comes next for Harborside United.
“We take it one game at a time — I know everybody says that, but the moment you look two fixtures ahead is the moment you drop points,” the manager said.
On the title race: “The table looks kind today, but 5 games is a long time in this league. Our jobs are won on cold nights against sides fighting for their lives.”
Asked about the squad's depth, there was a smile: “Competition for places is the best coach I have.”
The message to supporters was simple: keep coming, keep singing, and judge us in May.
